slides.heading: Combining Comparisons
slides.body: Combining Comparisons is part of Boolean Logic and Comparisons. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Combining Comparisons
slides.body: Multiple comparisons can be combined to check ranges or complex rules. Parentheses can make the logic easier to read.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: Combining comparisons is like checking a scholarship requirement: grade, documents, and deadline must all be considered.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Boolean expressions must produce True or False. Use comparisons and logical operators carefully.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Check whether age is between 13 and 19 inclusive.

quiz.prompt_text: What does the expression score >= 75 and score <= 100 check?

options: Whether score is exactly 75 or exactly 100
Whether score is between 75 and 100 inclusive
Whether score is either less than 75 or greater than 100

quiz.explanation: Correct! The expression uses and to combine two comparisons, checking that score is at least 75 AND no more than 100 — a range check.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to assign a score and check if it is in the passing range.
quiz.explanation: The comment is first, then score is assigned, and finally the combined comparison checks both conditions at once inside print().

quiz.prompt_text: Check whether age is between 13 and 19 inclusive and print the result.

content.hint: Use age >= 13 and age <= 19 inside a print() call.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(age >= 13 and age <= 19) outputs True for age = 16. Combining comparisons with and is the standard way to check if a value falls within a range.
